payload.because: Measured this session on the installed binary (N=15, mean): `sofar event append` costs 61.5ms, of which 50.5ms is process spawn plus full-bundle parse and only ~11ms is the actual record work; an MCP call on the already-running server costs that ~11ms alone. The CLI path also spawns a SECOND process, because the PostToolUse matcher is Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash and never matches mcp__sofar__*, so every Bash-issued sofar command fires a hook that reads the command, applies the record-hygiene D1 self-recording exemption and appends nothing. End to end that is ~92ms across 2 processes against ~11ms across 0 — roughly 8x. Correctness decides it independently of speed: `sofar event append` resolves by branch alone and never consults the session home (record-integrity M1, and AppendArgs.slug documents it), so on this shared worktree, where peers rebind branches mid-session, the CLI path can misroute the write that this initiative exists to make reliable. Precedent agrees — task status has no CLI writer either. The existing dual-path commands are dual because they touch bindings.json or the git branch, which an MCP call cannot sensibly do; phase status touches nothing outside the log. Benchmark: scratchpad/bench-paths.sh.

payload.because: (c) was already the trap; 0.26.0 doubled its cost. Before, derivation destroyed one axis — doctor's stale-phase check. The close audit shipped in 0.26.0 added a second independent reader: closeout.ts's `phases_unresolved` finding (closeout.ts:35, :93-99) compares phase.status against nothing but itself. Derive it and BOTH axes become tautologies that can never fire, so the record permanently loses the sentence 35 phases in this repo are trying to say right now: every task resolved, the phase itself was never finished. (b) fails on expressiveness, not cost. Phase status is not a function of task status: pending→active corresponds to no task event at all; a phase deliberately resolved over one outstanding task, or dropped wholesale, cannot be said through a task write; and a two-headed update_task means a phase is only ever resolvable as a side effect of its last task — the same derivation defect wearing a tool's clothes. The defect is now consequential and accruing, not cosmetic: sofar's own most recent close ate it. commit-attribution closed 2026-08-13T13:44:19Z carrying overrides[0] "3 phases never resolved: Phase 2 — Write and read the trailer (active), Phase 3 — Derive shipped state (active), Phase 5 — Close gate + contracts (pending)" — permanent by contract (events.ts:88-93 keeps close overrides in the digest forever) and false as history, since all three were finished and only unsayable. Doctor counts 35 such phases across 16 initiatives today, up from 32/15 this morning; the +3 are exactly those. Every initiative that closes before this tool ships earns the same permanent scar.

payload.text: Correction to D3's premise, measured after logging it. D3 says this change makes phase_status_changed "routinely WRITTEN for the first time". Wrong: the event is already routine through the MCP-less dialect. 70 of them exist across this repo's record — 40 from claude-code sessions, 30 from `sofar event append` — spanning 19 of 37 initiatives, all in the week from 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-13. D3's ruling is unaffected and in fact stronger than argued: those 70 mutations were ALL invisible to freshness, so the drift the Stop gate reads has been under-counting phase work for a week, not merely about to. What the missing tool cost was never emission — it was uniformity: 18 initiatives never emitted one at all, and 35 finished phases are still unresolved. The fold.ts comment on the `phases` counter carries the corrected number.

Three events in the whole 37-initiative record — harness-build 12.4 (2026-07-10), harness-build 13.1 (2026-07-11), task-drop-state 3.3 (2026-08-05) — all appended through the MCP-less dialect, all folded correctly, and 12.4/13.1 still render in harness-build's plan today. Against task_status_changed's 382, plan_updated's 80 and phase_status_changed's 70, that is roughly one use per four months. So there is no defect here to fix: nothing is stuck, no surface renders the wrong thing, and the one path that exists has never failed. Compare what this initiative DID find — 35 finished phases still rendering as live work, the digest's Current and Next task lines silently gone in 14 records because status.ts scopes them to the active phase, and a permanent close-time override on the last initiative to close. That is the standard a twelfth tool has to meet. The cost of missing it is not zero either: SPEC calls the MCP surface frozen and a test asserts its exact size, because every tool is context every session pays for on every call. Re-open this only on evidence — the strongest candidate is a MEASURED case of plan_updated's full replace clobbering a concurrent session's task edits on a shared worktree, which would make granular task addition a correctness fix rather than a symmetry.

payload.because: The "leave it as history" reading mistakes what the event says. A phase_status_changed appended today does not claim the phase finished today; it records that today someone stated its status, which is exactly true, and the log keeps both the statement and its time. Rewriting the original events WOULD be a fiction, and that is the thing ruled out. The cost of leaving them is not cosmetic: status.ts scopes the digest's Current task and Next task lines to the active phase, so in every record whose active phase is a finished one those two lines — the most-read lines of the orientation block — are silently absent. That is 14 of the 16 records rendering degraded digests at every session start. A shipped `doctor --fix` is rejected on the standing rule that doctor never touches record prose (SPEC §CLI): the fix is a JUDGEMENT about whether work is finished, and a flag that makes that judgement for you is how a record stops meaning anything. Two hazards make this a phase of work rather than a script, and Phase 4 owes an answer to both: writing to another initiative with an explicit `initiative` argument TEARS the calling session (statusline-refresh M1), and the CLI's `sofar event append` resolves by branch alone, never consulting the session home (record-integrity M1). A repair that tears itself across 16 records is worse than the defect it clears.

The actual bundles are dist/fast.js (~170 KB, the hot path) and dist/full.js (~1.2 MB, everything else). esbuild also strips comments, so verify with a code or string literal, never with a comment you just wrote.

payload.because: (c) fails on the one risk that matters. Phase names are free text and applyEvent's findOrCreatePhase CREATES one on a miss — the right call for a fold that must never lose a fact, and the wrong one here. harness-build already carries that scar at line 204 ("Phase 13 - Sync contract", created implicitly). This pass hand-carries 35 names, most containing an em dash, through shell JSON quoting into records it is reading concurrently; a slip mints a phantom phase that renders in someone else's plan forever, and the repair for a stale-phase count would have raised it. sofar_update_phase validates the name against the folded plan and errors typed, and takes the string as a JSON arg with no shell in the path — which is precisely why 2.3 built that check. (a) buys the same validation and pays for it with a permanent 17-way tear on the record that shipped the tool. The known cost of the chosen path is accepted and stated: 16 records get a bookkeeping entry in their digest's "Last session" slot. That entry earns its place — it is what explains to the next agent why a phase finished in July carries an August close.

payload.text:
A cross-record bookkeeping session MUST carry the target record's existing next action forward VERBATIM. sofar_end_session's next_action REPLACES whatever the record had — there is no merge and no append — so a session that writes into another initiative for a mechanical reason (a phase close, a status repair) and then writes back with its own next action has silently destroyed that record's real one. Nothing warns: the write-back succeeds, the digest renders, and the loss is only visible to someone who remembers what used to be there.

The discipline that makes it safe, used across all 16 records of the phase-lifecycle 4.3 repair: read `Next action:` off the target's plan.md BEFORE writing anything, and pass that string back unchanged. Put your own account of the visit in the `summary`, which has no such alias, and put any observation about the next action being stale in the summary too — never in the field itself. Editing another record's next action is a judgement belonging to that record's owner, even when you can see it is out of date.

Two traps ride along with it:
1. A token starting with `--` anywhere in end_session's args makes the write-back fail with a misleading "next_action: must be a non-empty string". cli-ui's next action contains `sofar status --watch`, so preserving it verbatim through the MCP tool is IMPOSSIBLE. The fallback that works and preserves bytes exactly: `sofar event append <slug> --type session_ended --session <id> --source claude-code --actor agent --payload '{"session_id":…,"summary":…,"next_action":…}'` — one JSON string sidesteps the multi-arg handling. Note the explicit <slug>, which is what keeps that CLI write off the branch resolver (record-integrity M1).
2. session_ended is LAST-WINS, so a write-back with a mangled next action is repairable: append another one with the correct text and the projection re-renders. Verified live this session after paraphrasing commit-attribution's publish command instead of preserving it.
